Name: Barks_01_WatchmanDozeStart
speaker: Watchman
line: The king slew the last of 'em, so what exactly am I watching for… mmnh.
note: The doze is a timer on his perception cone; the propaganda is the excuse he naps on, so the nap and the joke are the same beat.

Name: Barks_02_WatchmanDozeEnd
speaker: Watchman
line: Awake! Watching! Been watching this whole time — what time is it?
note: Fires as the drooping vision cone snaps back up, telling the player the nap window just closed without a HUD readout.

Name: Barks_03_CoinTossScramble
speaker: Guard
line: Ooh — dropped coin, no owner, that's salvage, that's mine by law.
note: The coin toss works on guards because greed is the exploitable stat; he breaks off his post and legally justifies it to himself.

Name: Barks_04_CoinTossScramble
speaker: Civilian
line: Coins in the mud at the king's feet — the statue's paying out!
note: Uses the village-centre statue of the king from the propaganda dressing, and keeps civilian greed on the same branch as guard greed.

Name: Barks_05_FlockStartledInvestigate
speaker: Guard
line: Squawk all you like, hens — it's a fox, it's always a fox, it has never once not been a fox.
note: A startled flock is a soft signal that pulls the nearest guard to investigate; he investigates while pre-explaining it away.

Name: Barks_06_FlockStartledNearbyRoutine
speaker: Civilian
line: A goblin? In my pen? Don't be daft, it's shearing day.
note: The GDD's own reference bark, sitting on the flock noise event — disbelief first, chores uninterrupted.

Name: Barks_07_CorpseDiscovered
speaker: Guard
line: Somebody's knifed the pen-hand. …Right. That's a fox with a knife. Investigating.
note: Seeing a body goes only to Suspicious, never straight to the bell, because the denial is doing the work.

Name: Barks_08_CorpseDiscoveredSecond
speaker: Guard
line: Second body. Badger with ambition, that's — no. No. BELL! RING THE BELL!
note: A second soft signal while the hamlet is already SUSPICIOUS escalates straight to RAID, so the denial breaks mid-sentence — which is exactly where the joke lands.

Name: Barks_09_SightingConfirmed
speaker: Guard
line: Green. Waist-high. Grinning. …I am not writing that in the book.
note: Fires the moment a sighting holds long enough to confirm; disbelief, not fear, is the first reaction to an extinct monster.

Name: Barks_10_SoftSignalDecayReturnToQuiet
speaker: Guard
line: No goblin, no tracks, no nothing — trick of the light, back to your chores.
note: The audible tell that an uncorroborated soft signal has decayed back to Quiet, since no timer shows on the HUD.

Name: Barks_11_RoutineResumeAfterDecay
speaker: Civilian
line: Must've been a badger. A badger wearing a belt. Badgers do that.
note: Post-decay pottering resumes; canon's badger line, pushed one notch dumber because the villager did in fact see a belt.

Name: Barks_12_PatrolOverdueNoCheckIn
speaker: Guard
line: That patrol's well past its waypoint — three grown soldiers lost on a road with signposts on it.
note: The ambient mutter that a patrol is running late is the only tell the missing-patrol soft signal has fired.

Name: Barks_13_HornWindUpPatrolLosing
speaker: PatrolArcher
line: We're losing — horn, horn, I'm sounding the — EXTINCT, ARE THEY?!
note: She only winds up the horn once the patrol is losing; the committed wind-up is the player's window to cut her down.

Name: Barks_14_WellFouledDiscovered
speaker: Civilian
line: There's something in the well, and I think it's looking back at me!
note: Sells the +30 well-fouling counterplay as a readable, disgusting event rather than a stat change.

Name: Barks_15_BucketBrigadeFormUp
speaker: Militia
line: Bucket line, move! Well to the granary — pass it up, don't spill it!
note: The clean-well case: bucket lines form at the well in RAID and run water to a burning objective, so the player hears exactly what fouling the well would have cost them.

Name: Barks_16_BucketBrigadeDisabledWellFou
speaker: Civilian
line: The granary's alight and the well's gone foul — we're fighting fire with soup!
note: The audible confirmation that fouling the well permanently killed the brigade, tied to a burning objective.

Name: Barks_17_LastPushHamletBurning
speaker: Militia
line: Windmill's ash, field's ash, fine — FINE — goblins! I said it! Are we happy?!
note: At RAZED the denial finally snaps; the punchline lands on the man who spent the whole raid telling it.

Name: Barks_18_RoutinesGoneQuiet
speaker: Civilian
line: Nobody at the pens, nobody in the field — nobody left to tell me it was a badger.
note: A hamlet's worth of empty routines is the strained denial's final beat, and it reads the same whether the missing were killed or bound.
